notes: Dev TBox contraction, paired with grammar-replace-d005: it removes that revision's original rule, 'In German spelling, every noun is written with a capital initial letter', which every model holds and which has no exception in standard orthography. Its own questions are the revision's, asked of the original rule; under strong Kleene the three propositional answers are unknown. The three derived queries state the membership in the prompt (inheritance, 2 hops): a rare compound (Zahnbürstenhalter, 19 Dolma hits), a second rare compound (Briefmarkensammlerverein, 13 hits), and an application that counts the capitals of a lowercase sentence. Before the removal the rule gives the capital (and 2 capitals in the sentence); after it nothing the model holds about these rare words settles their case, so all three become 'does not know'. The words are shown in lowercase because showing them capitalised would give the original answer away. Residual risk: the rule is so famous that a model may keep it through stored examples (das Buch) or a separate rule for nominalised words; a capital after the removal is then the rule kept by another route. Near unrelated: the capital of the polite pronoun 'Sie', a capitalisation rule outside the noun class (delete is exempt from Rule 7).
